reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Prime DeFi as a way to earn 60%–120% or more in yearly passive crypto income and presents profit as effectively assured. The host reinforces the solicitation with testimonials, claims that people who take action get results, directs viewers to start through a linked free training, and says Dan Ryder will ensure participants are in profit. These claims and calls to participate promote a high-return DeFi earning opportunity rather than neutrally analyzing it.

showing investors how to earn 60 or more passively safely
he even has guarantees like he will make sure that you will be in the profit
so go ahead get started today and finally crush it with crypto
Want the FREE training from Dan Ryder? Learn how people are earning 3%–10% per month WITHOUT trading

opening.argument: Judge, the return figures should be read alongside the speaker's qualifications, not as a promise that every viewer will earn them. After describing individual outcomes, he explicitly says results will differ and depend on what someone does. The description also discloses the channel's affiliate-link practice. Those qualifications matter when assessing whether the video presents earnings as certain, even if its enthusiasm deserves scrutiny.

citations.quote: now i'm not gonna say everyone's gonna have the same kind of results it all depends on how much action you want to take
Disclaimers: all opinions are my own, sponsors are acknowledged. Links in the description are typically affiliate links that let you help support the channel at no extra cost.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes the claim that Dan will make sure participants are in profit, but that is the host's account of support from Dan, not a set of terms establishing a fixed return. It also omits the host's express warning that testimonial results will not be the same for everyone. The invitation to training is promotional; it does not erase that qualification.

citations.quote: he even has guarantees like he will make sure that you will be in the profit he'll work with you
now i'm not gonna say everyone's gonna have the same kind of results it all depends on how much action you want to take

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The results-vary sentence does not neutralize the direct assurance that Dan will make sure participants are in profit. Nor does an affiliate disclosure make the earning claims less promotional. The description advertises monthly returns beside an invitation to enter the free training, and the host tells viewers to get started. Those are the operative messages, not merely qualified market commentary.

opening.argument: Judge, this is presented as an examination of a training program and what it teaches. The description says the host will cover the program, its testimonials, intended audience, and whether joining is worthwhile. The instruction described includes risk management, withdrawal planning, and portfolio coaching, not just a return figure. The host also situates this video within his practice of reviewing opportunities and calling out schemes. That context supports reading the earning examples as subjects of a review rather than the entirety of its purpose.

citations.quote: What Prime DeFi actually teaches
cash flow strategies uh is in his program risk management automation compounding tax and withdrawal strategies personal portfolio coaching
i call out the garbage out there i've been doing reviews for several years now

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution focuses on the strongest sales lines, but its quotations do not capture the program discussion around them. The host identifies risk management, tax and withdrawal strategies, and coaching as subjects of the training. A favorable review can contain a call to learn more without every discussion of potential returns becoming a standalone investment solicitation.

citations.quote: cash flow strategies uh is in his program risk management automation compounding tax and withdrawal strategies personal portfolio coaching
What Prime DeFi actually teaches

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The review format does not change what the host urges viewers to do. He says people who follow the training and calls do well, says Dan will ensure they are in profit, and directs viewers to get started. The curriculum list is embedded in a pitch for a recurring-income opportunity, not an operational demonstration that displaces the pitch.

opening.argument: Judge, the identifiable transaction being promoted here is access to training and coaching. The description invites viewers to free training, while the host describes live calls, an app for evaluating whether to invest, and personal portfolio coaching. The supplied account does not show a viewer being asked to hand over credentials or transfer funds to a named pool. Its affiliate-link disclosure gives a conventional explanation for why the reviewer directs traffic to the offer. Those limits do not prove the service is sound, but they matter before treating the video as evidence of a specific deposit scheme.

citations.quote: Want the FREE training from Dan Ryder?
attend the live calls use this app by the way that shows you okay should you invest in this or not
personal portfolio coaching
Links in the description are typically affiliate links that let you help support the channel at no extra cost.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution establishes that the host promotes striking returns and a start-now pathway. It does not establish from those quotes that the host collects deposits, requests credentials, or specifies a pool into which viewers must place funds. The linked offer is described as free training. Judge the claims critically, but do not infer an unseen transaction from the strength of the endorsement alone.

citations.quote: Want the FREE training from Dan Ryder? Learn how people are earning 3%–10% per month WITHOUT trading
so go ahead get started today and finally crush it with crypto

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A direct deposit instruction is not needed to see what the video promotes. It links DeFi yield strategies to claimed annual earnings, offers a training pathway promising monthly earnings, and tells viewers to get started while saying Dan will ensure profit. Calling the first step free does not make the recurring-return pitch ordinary service advertising.
